doc: Ten rows of the same synoptic row with different targets and streaks, no subtexel, offset 0.0. Row 0: target 0.5, interior. Row 1: target 0.0, the root is the smallest t with a cloud-free row, max(s) + cumulus_depth. Row 2: target 1.0 with a streak that dips the shield: unreachable, the mean is never above the target so the result runs down to the lower bound (about -10). Row 3: 0.95 with streak = +1 (shield capped at 0.7, coverage at 0.94): unreachable, lower bound. Row 4: target 1.0 with streak = -1, where the row IS exactly 1 at low t: mean > 1 is never true (strict comparison), so again the lower bound. Row 5: 0.999 with streak -1, reachable, near min(s) - 0.175 where the first texel leaves full shield. Rows 6 and 7: targets 1.2 and -0.2 (lower bound -10 and upper bound +10). Row 8: a small reachable 0.02. Row 9: 0.97 with streak -1, reachable. The bounds are exact up to the final bracket 20 / 2^36 (the result is the bracket midpoint); the target of rows 1 and 4 is exact, a port must compare strictly (>) in float64. Arguments: s, fine, target, streak, subtexel and offset are the inputs of that name when listed; an unlisted streak or offset (default 0.0) is the scalar in params, an unlisted subtexel is None; prm holds the GenParams fields compose reads. The 36 steps and the bracket [-10, 10] are literals of the source. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 5.5e-9; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 2.4e-7 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is about 1e2x the larger of the two spreads.
